# FDG7051

> DO prefer catching `OperationCanceledException` to `TaskCanceledException`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.3.9 OperationCanceledException and TaskCanceledException.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG7051
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Message: Catch OperationCanceledException instead of TaskCanceledException

FDG7051 reports a catch clause whose type is System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException, unless the same try statement also catches OperationCanceledException, which the body accepts as the other handling. A type test in a filter is not seen, so coverage is partial. There is no code fix: catching the base type catches more exceptions.

## From the book

`TaskCanceledException` derives from `OperationCanceledException`. The type is used internally by the Task execution engine, but otherwise is barely distinguishable from the parent type. Catch blocks that have special handling for `TaskCanceledException` should generally also have handling for `OperationCanceledException`.
